ca-grade4-multidigit.fit: Multi-digit addition and subtraction practice after an introduction to regrouping.
ca-grade4-multidigit.prerequisites: Read whole numbers to 100,000 and identify place values.
ca-grade4-multidigit.model: Model 40,003 - 18,756 = 21,247. Rename across the zeros, subtract by place, then check that 21,247 + 18,756 = 40,003.
ca-grade4-multidigit.misconception: Subtracting the smaller digit from the larger digit in each column ignores place value. Ask the learner to show the renamed number.

supports.AIG: Create two different subtraction problems with the same difference and justify both.
supports.504: Offer chunked tasks, reduced copying, extra time, and breaks as specified in the learner’s plan.
supports.EC: Use a place-value chart and counters to represent regrouping before recording digits.
supports.ESL: Rehearse: I regrouped one ___ as ten ___. Preteach sum, difference, and estimate.

exitItems: Solve 60,002 - 24,785. Show regrouping.
Check your difference using addition and explain why the check works.
exitAnswers: 35,217. The written work must preserve place value through the zeros.
35,217 + 24,785 = 60,002. Addition reverses subtraction.

fl-grade5-theme.fit: A focused lesson on how a theme develops across one original story.
fl-grade5-theme.prerequisites: Identify characters, a problem, and the sequence of events.
fl-grade5-theme.model: Contrast a topic (teamwork) with a theme (accepting help can turn a setback into progress). Trace Mina restarting, accepting paint, and sharing the finished sign.
fl-grade5-theme.misconception: A theme is not a one-word topic or a plot summary. Require a general lesson and evidence from more than one part of the story.

supports.AIG: Defend a second plausible theme using different evidence from the same text.
supports.504: Offer chunked tasks, reduced copying, extra time, and breaks as specified in the learner’s plan.
supports.EC: Use a three-box beginning/middle/end organizer and rehearse the explanation aloud.
supports.ESL: Rehearse: At first ___. Later ___. By the end ___. These changes suggest ___.

exitItems: State a theme of The Garden Sign as a complete sentence.
Explain how an early event and the ending develop that theme.
exitAnswers: Possible: Accepting help while persisting through setbacks can lead to shared success. Other defensible themes are acceptable.

For example, Mina first tries to repair the sign alone, then accepts neighbors’ materials and help; carrying it together at the end shows her change. Credit accurate evidence and an explicit connection.

tx-grade7-elements-compounds.fit: Paper-based comparison of elements, compounds, symbols, and particle descriptions. No laboratory equipment is required.
tx-grade7-elements-compounds.prerequisites: Recognize an atom and read simple element symbols.
tx-grade7-elements-compounds.model: Compare O₂ and CO₂: O₂ has two atoms of one element; CO₂ has three atoms of two elements. Count kinds of atoms before classifying. NaCl represents a ratio in an ionic compound, not a discrete molecule.
tx-grade7-elements-compounds.misconception: More than one atom does not automatically mean compound. The number of different elements matters.

supports.AIG: Explain why both O₂ and O₃ are elements even though their molecules differ.
supports.504: Offer chunked tasks, reduced copying, extra time, and breaks as specified in the learner’s plan.
supports.EC: Use labeled counters for atom types; keep labels as well as colors.
supports.ESL: Rehearse: This is a ___ because it contains ___ kind(s) of atom.

exitItems: Classify N₂ and CO₂ as element or compound. Explain each.
Consider two separate water molecules (H₂O). How many H and O atoms are present in total?
exitAnswers: N₂ is an element (nitrogen only). CO₂ is a compound (carbon and oxygen chemically combined).
Four hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms. Each H₂O molecule contains two H and one O.

college-composition-claims.fit: A short first-year writing workshop on claims, evidence, and reasoning.
college-composition-claims.prerequisites: Write complete paragraphs and distinguish fact from opinion.
college-composition-claims.model: Use the fictional 68-of-100 survey as evidence of this sample’s evening library use. Explain why it supports considering later hours, but does not establish what all students need.
college-composition-claims.misconception: Repeating a statistic is not analysis; a small fictional sample is not a real campus research finding.

supports.AIG: Develop an alternative explanation and propose better evidence to test it.
supports.504: Offer chunked tasks, reduced copying, extra time, and breaks as specified in the learner’s plan.
supports.EC: Use separate claim, evidence, and reasoning boxes before combining a paragraph.
supports.ESL: Rehearse: This evidence supports ___ because ___. A limitation is ___.

exitItems: A fictional survey finds that 12 of 20 evening students use a tutoring center. Write a cautious claim supported by this sample.
Explain one limitation and what additional evidence would strengthen the claim.
exitAnswers: Example: Tutoring is used by a majority of the surveyed evening students. Avoid a claim about all students or about causes.
The sample is small and may be unrepresentative. A larger, more representative survey or usage records would strengthen the evidence.

college-algebra-linear.fit: Introductory algebra review of constant-rate models, not a complete college algebra course.
college-algebra-linear.prerequisites: Solve one-step equations and interpret ordered pairs.
college-algebra-linear.model: For C(h)=18+6h, identify the $18 starting fee and $6 per hour. Set 18+6h=72, subtract 18, then divide by 6 to get 9 hours.
college-algebra-linear.misconception: The intercept is the starting cost, not the hourly rate. Units should appear in interpretations.

supports.AIG: Compare two pricing models and identify when each costs less.
supports.504: Offer chunked tasks, reduced copying, extra time, and breaks as specified in the learner’s plan.
supports.EC: Use a table for h=0,1,2 before writing the rule; annotate units.
supports.ESL: Rehearse: Each additional hour changes cost by ___. At zero hours, ___.

exitItems: A rental costs $12 plus $4 per hour. Write C(h), then find C(5).
For this model, how many hours cost $40? Explain the meaning of the solution.
exitAnswers: 12+4h=40 gives h=7 hours. Seven hours of rental costs $40 under this pricing rule.

college-biology-membranes.fit: Concept review of membrane transport using simplified concentration scenarios.
college-biology-membranes.prerequisites: Identify a membrane, solute, solvent, and concentration.
college-biology-membranes.model: Assume water crosses but the solute cannot. With 2% solute inside and 8% outside, net water movement is out. State this permeability assumption before predicting.
college-biology-membranes.misconception: Tonicity depends on nonpenetrating solutes; a percentage comparison alone is incomplete without membrane assumptions.

supports.AIG: Explain how the prediction changes if the solute crosses the membrane freely.
supports.504: Offer chunked tasks, reduced copying, extra time, and breaks as specified in the learner’s plan.
supports.EC: Draw a labeled membrane and arrows; count particles using the same volume on each side.
supports.ESL: Rehearse: Net water moves ___ because the nonpenetrating solute concentration is ___.

exitItems: A cell has 3% nonpenetrating solute; the solution has 1%. Water can cross. Predict net water movement.
A carrier moves solute against its gradient using energy. Identify the transport type and explain.
exitAnswers: Water moves into the cell; the external solution is hypotonic under the stated assumptions.
Active transport. Movement against the gradient requires an energy source.

college-psych-research.fit: Introductory review of research designs, variables, and ethical reasoning.
college-psych-research.prerequisites: Distinguish a measured outcome from a proposed explanation.
college-psych-research.model: In a randomized fictional experiment comparing quiet and music study conditions, sound condition is the independent variable and quiz score is the dependent variable.
college-psych-research.misconception: Random assignment supports group comparability; random sampling supports population representation. They serve different purposes.

supports.AIG: Identify a confound and redesign the study to reduce it.
supports.504: Offer chunked tasks, reduced copying, extra time, and breaks as specified in the learner’s plan.
supports.EC: Sort short examples into manipulated variable, measured outcome, and uncontrolled factor.
supports.ESL: Rehearse: The researchers change ___ and measure ___. This design can/cannot ___.

exitItems: Students choose whether to attend tutoring. Attendees score higher. Does this prove tutoring caused higher scores? Explain.
For a randomized study of quiet versus music, identify the independent and dependent variables if the outcome is quiz score.
exitAnswers: No. Self-selection and other differences, such as motivation or prior knowledge, may explain the association.
Independent variable: sound condition. Dependent variable: quiz score.

spanish101-campus.fit: Beginning Spanish practice with introductions and present-tense forms.
spanish101-campus.prerequisites: Recognize Spanish subject pronouns and basic greetings.
spanish101-campus.model: Model: Buenos días. Me llamo Ana. Soy estudiante. Estudio español. Show how -ar becomes -o for yo and -a for ella/él/usted.
spanish101-campus.misconception: Match verb endings to the subject; formal usted uses third-person singular forms.

supports.AIG: Extend a dialogue to include a formal introduction and a plural response.
supports.504: Offer chunked tasks, reduced copying, extra time, and breaks as specified in the learner’s plan.
supports.EC: Provide a subject-pronoun/verb-ending chart and practice one sentence at a time.
supports.ESL: Use a bilingual phrase bank, then rehearse a brief exchange with a partner.

exitItems: Complete: Yo ___ español. (estudiar) Nosotros ___ estudiantes. (ser)
Write a formal question asking someone their name, followed by an appropriate answer.
exitAnswers: estudio; somos.
¿Cómo se llama usted? Me llamo ___. Accept an appropriate name and correct verb form.

college-accounting-cycle.fit: Foundational accounting-equation practice with a single sequence of transactions.
college-accounting-cycle.prerequisites: Identify assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses.
college-accounting-cycle.model: Owner investment of $8,000 increases cash and owner equity equally. Buying equipment for $1,200 cash changes asset composition, not total assets.
college-accounting-cycle.misconception: A cash payment is not always an expense: purchasing equipment exchanges one asset for another.

supports.AIG: Add a new transaction that changes assets and liabilities without changing equity.
supports.504: Offer chunked tasks, reduced copying, extra time, and breaks as specified in the learner’s plan.
supports.EC: Use an Assets = Liabilities + Equity table with one row per transaction.
supports.ESL: Rehearse: ___ increases/decreases by ___, so the equation stays balanced.

exitItems: Starting from zero, an owner invests $2,000 cash and buys $300 supplies on account. Find assets, liabilities, and equity.
The business pays $100 of the amount owed. Recalculate all three totals.
exitAnswers: Assets $2,300; liabilities $300; equity $2,000.
Assets $2,200; liabilities $200; equity $2,000. Cash and accounts payable each decrease $100.

college-programming-python.fit: Paper-based Python 3 tracing and conditional practice; a Python interpreter is optional.
college-programming-python.model: Trace x=3. The condition x>5 is False, so the else branch doubles x to 6. Emphasize that only one branch runs and indentation defines the block.
college-programming-python.misconception: Use == to compare and = to assign. elif and else belong on separate lines with correctly indented bodies.

supports.AIG: Add a boundary case and explain whether the threshold should use > or >=.
supports.504: Offer chunked tasks, reduced copying, extra time, and breaks as specified in the learner’s plan.
supports.EC: Use a trace table with columns for line, condition, and variable value.
supports.ESL: Rehearse: The condition is ___, so the program executes ___ and outputs ___.

exitItems: If score is 75, what does this rule print: print("pass" if score >= 70 else "retry")? Explain.
Write a Boolean condition that is True when age is at least 18 and has_id is True.
exitAnswers: pass, because 75 >= 70 is True.
age >= 18 and has_id (or age >= 18 and has_id == True).
